series: Things Living In Your House, Part 15
sources: University of California IPM, Drain flies (Moth flies, Pest Notes 7487): small fuzzy flies about 1/8 inch, wings held roof-like over the body and covered with hairs; weak fliers that make short hopping flights; larvae live in the gelatinous film in drains and feed on the organic material and microorganisms in it; larvae breathe through a tube at the rear end; to find the source, tape over drains overnight and look for flies on the tape; the best control is cleaning the film out with a stiff brush, pouring chemicals down the drain is usually not effective; they do not bite; https://ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/PESTNOTES/pn7487.html

Penn State Extension, Moth flies (drain flies): females lay 30-100 eggs in the drain film; the life cycle takes about 8 to 24 days; adults live about two weeks; also called filter flies because they breed in huge numbers in sewage treatment trickling filters; https://extension.psu.edu/moth-flies

title: The Fuzzy Fly on Your Bathroom Wall Grew Up in Your Drain 🚿
tiktok_caption: the fuzzy little fly on my bathroom wall grew up inside my drain 🚿 and its babies breathe through a snorkel. Would you check your drain tonight? 🔦 yes / 🙈 no way

beats.say: That fuzzy fly on your bathroom wall? It grew up in your drain.
The drain fly. Fuzzy wings, shaped like a heart.
It barely flies. It just hops along the wall.
Mom lays up to a hundred eggs.
Right in the slime inside your drain.
The babies are tiny worms that eat the slime.
And they breathe through a snorkel on their butt.
Your drain is basically a fly nursery.
